Plan for Phase 12 / B4, docs only (Jack: no code in this handoff). Uncommitted on branch docs/per-user-cloud-keys off main b2078bb. Files: new `docs/phases/per-user-cloud-keys.md`; the Phase 12 entry in `docs/roadmap.md`.

The plan covers both repos. Bugalizer builds B4 here. Sonicgrid builds S3 (AI settings) and S4 (the bug board) in its own tagteam; its code is at ~/Projects/sonic/sonicgrid if you want to check the touchpoints the plan names.

What it plans:
(1) One six-lane board replaces sonicgrid's /admin/bugs tabs: Submitted, In triage, Triaged, In fix, In review, Completed, with a single status and basic styling borrowed from Bugalizer's dashboard. Bugalizer computes the lane and pushes it as `stage` / `stageDetail` / `prState`.
(2) Each admin's own Claude key and default model, on an Aegis-style settings page. Sonicgrid encrypts it (AES-GCM, AAD = user id). Bugalizer fetches it once per claimed paid action through a new credential endpoint and uses Phase 7's per-request override. The model is pinned in the action params at queue time. The allowlist is retired.
(3) Bugalizer polls each fix PR's state on GitHub. Merged → closed (pr_merged); closed unmerged → triaged. Plus a `reopen` action.

Decisions F1–F7 are Jack's from today's brainstorm, recorded in the doc. Please review in particular:
- The lane/stageDetail mapping and its precedence (§1).
- The credential endpoint's one-time release, and how it interacts with Phase 11 recovery and no_auto_retry (§4).
- The contract-first sequencing: sonicgrid's result schema is strict (§Contract changes, §Sequencing).
- The status transitions the plan says may need workflow-engine changes (§2, §3, Risks).
- Whether anything here conflicts with the Phase 11 contract or the Phase 7 secrecy rules.

Not verified: Anthropic's actual commercial terms on end-user keys. Only secondary sources were read; this is flagged as a risk to check before S3b. No tests run (docs only).

Plan review: REQUEST_CHANGES. Reviewed docs/phases/per-user-cloud-keys.md, the roadmap diff, current Bugalizer PR finalization/state machine/result builder/action dispatch, and sonicgrid's endpoint contract, queue action, result route and revision-gated SQL upsert. No code changes or tests (docs-only turn). No interjections or standing orders were delivered. F1-F7 are treated as the accepted product decisions; the changes below make their implementation consistent with the existing systems.

1. [P1] Correct the PR lifecycle against the actual Phase 8 states (§1-2, lines 62-79). Opening a PR already writes fix_committed: db._record_pr_report and record_pull_request explicitly finalize fix_approved -> fix_committed. Public PATCH gating does not mean that state is unused. Polling only fix_proposed misses normal opened PRs, while placing fix_committed in Completed resolves bugs before merge. Put an open recorded PR in Review, poll its actual owning proposal/report, and specify fix_committed -> closed on merge and -> triaged on unmerged close. Define durable storage for prState/last check and the one-time terminal transition/note, including restart behavior and CAS against concurrent manual changes. Add an end-to-end plan test that opens a PR through the real Phase 8 finalization, observes Review/open, and only then reaches Completed/merged or Triaged/closed. Also define how an explicit reopen of a previously merged bug avoids being immediately closed again from the same historical PR.

2. [P2] Make triaged detail precedence expose actionable states (§1, lines 59-65). The written ordering puts localized/stale/not_localized before held and fix_failed. Nearly every triaged report satisfies one of those localization conditions, so held and fix_failed are effectively hidden; notably a permanently interrupted fix with fresh localization will show localized instead of its failure. Specify complete predicates and an intentional priority for failure/hold versus localization, including how a newer successful fix clears an old failure. Clarify the analyzing fallback before a running row exists. Add overlap cases: held+localized, failed fix+localized, failed fix+stale, and recovered success after failure.

3. [P1] Finish the one-time credential and dispatch state contract (§4). 'Transport failure is transient under the existing action timeout' is not implemented by today's dispatcher: _dispatch records dispatched before _run_task, and _run_task terminalizes exceptions. Specify durable intent/dispatched ordering relative to credential fetch, exact outcomes for a lost credential response, timeout before/after release, 409 already_released, and restart at each boundary. A successful fetch whose response is lost cannot simply be repeated under a one-release contract. Require atomic claimed/paid/unreleased validation plus release marking so concurrent endpoint requests cannot both receive a key; resolve the requester from the immutable action identity, never client input, and define key deletion/replacement/admin-revocation behavior while an action waits. Explicitly fail closed for absent/invalid params, non-Anthropic pins, empty/malformed credential responses, or provider mismatch: never construct a keyless override that falls back to the BOWIE env key. Add concurrent-release, lost-response, malformed-response/no-env-fallback, and crash-boundary tests. Preserve the existing no-auto-retry guarantee and compound-action consent/step semantics.

4. [P1] Make the single status follow confirmed, revision-ordered results (§3 and §5). Setting sonicgrid active when reopen is merely queued creates disagreement if the action fails, is refused, or never reaches Bugalizer. A delayed/retried completed result can also undo that optimistic update; today's SQL only gates the result row by revision. Define Bugalizer as the authority and update the sonicgrid status atomically with an accepted newer result (including returning to active for a successful reopen), or specify equivalent rollback and ordering rules. Rejected and duplicate remain completed and must not offer Reopen despite the generic Completed primary action. Include failed reopen, successful reopen, stale/duplicate completed pushes after reopen, and existing legacy active/resolved bugs without a stage. Name the result-upsert SQL/route changes in the file list.

5. [P2] Specify a safe mixed-version rollout (§Contract changes/Sequencing). S3a only accepts optional fields; before S3b the credential route does not exist and old paid actions have no provider/model params. That is different from an implemented endpoint returning no_key, so B4 is not merely inert as stated. Define deployment prerequisites or a feature gate, how pending old actions and already authorized in-flight/ledger actions are drained/refused, and when paid queueing and allowlist retirement switch together. S4 also queues reopen and depends on confirmed status updates, so schema acceptance alone is insufficient to enable all its actions. Require compatibility tests for old payloads, missing stage fields, missing credential route, and legacy paid actions; no compatibility path may silently spend the env key.

The explicitly unresolved Anthropic terms check can remain a release prerequisite before S3b; this review makes no claim that those terms have been verified. The Phase 7 in-memory key path, requester attribution, encrypted server-only storage direction, and contract-first approach are otherwise appropriate. Please revise the plan only and resubmit; implementation remains outside this turn.

r2: plan revised for all five findings. Docs only; still uncommitted on docs/per-user-cloud-keys. `docs/phases/per-user-cloud-keys.md` is rewritten. It adds three invariants that every section must keep: I1 no env-key fallback, I2 Bugalizer is the status authority, I3 no paid call twice per action.

1 (P1, PR lifecycle) — §1, §2. Confirmed: db.py:1349 finalizes fix_approved → fix_committed. Review now covers fix_proposed/fix_approved/fix_committed (`fix_ready`/`opening_pr`/`pr_open`); Completed covers closed/rejected/duplicate/verified. Durable `fix_proposals` columns `pr_state`, `pr_checked_at`, `pr_settled_at`. The poller selects `pr_settled_at IS NULL` on fix_committed reports. The terminal move is one transaction: a CAS `fix_committed → closed (pr_merged:<n>)` or `→ triaged`. On a CAS miss the state is still recorded and the status kept. Restart re-reads the PR, and the CAS makes a repeat harmless. Reopen after merge is never re-closed, because the proposal is settled. The e2e test goes through the real record_pull_request.

2 (P2, precedence) — §1. Full predicates. Priority: needs_clarification, deferred, held, fix_failed (newest fix row failed, newer than the newest completed localization, no newer proposal; cleared by a newer proposal or localization), pr_closed, stale, localized, not_localized. analyzing with no running row → `starting`. The overlap tests are listed.

3 (P1, credential/dispatch) — §4. A single UPDATE…WHERE claimed AND paid AND credential_released_at IS NULL RETURNING requested_by_user_id is the atomic release. The requester comes only from the row. Responses are defined for admin revocation, a deleted key and a replaced key. Authorization fails closed on absent/invalid params.llm or a non-Anthropic pin. Dispatch order inside _run_task (after `dispatched` is durable): fetch once; an outcome table covers 200 valid / malformed / mismatch / already_released / refusals / transport. A lost response is `failed` and never retried; the admin requests again. A new `propose_fix(require_request_key=True)` raises before any call (today a keyless override falls back to the env key; I confirmed that path). Compound fix-step mapping is specified. Crash boundaries: after dispatched → Phase 11 unconfirmed, so there is no second fetch.

4 (P1, single status) — §3, §5. Queueing reopen changes nothing in sonicgrid. upsert_bugalizer_result updates bug_reports.status only when the push is applied (newer revision): completed → resolved, other stages → active, no stage → unchanged. A stale completed push after a reopen is rejected by the revision gate. rejected/duplicate get no Reopen. Legacy and never-imported bugs keep the sonicgrid-local Resolve/Reopen and a static lane fallback. The migration, the route and the SQL tests are in the file list.

5 (P2, rollout) — new §Rollout. Ordered steps: S3a → B4 behind `BUGALIZER_SONICGRID_USER_KEYS` (off) → S3b → gate flip → S4 (any time after S3a; Reopen once B4 is live, refused before via the existing KINDS check). Drain rules at the flip: legacy paid actions without params, and old-mode ledger actions not yet dispatched, are refused; dispatched ones follow Phase 11 recovery. Nothing authorized under the old rules runs after the flip. Compatibility tests are listed. The allowlist code is deleted after one acceptance walk with the gate on.

Also fixed: sonicgrid column names checked against the migration (`requested_by_user_id`; the `kind` CHECK constraint gains `reopen`). The Anthropic terms check stays a release prerequisite for S3b. No code, no tests (docs only).

Plan r2 review: REQUEST_CHANGES for two remaining contract gaps. Docs only; no code edits or tests. Read the revised plan and submission, checked the existing close replay behavior in sync/actions.py, the Phase 11 inline recovery/dispatch path, and sonicgrid's action schema. No interjections or standing orders were delivered.

Round-1 findings 1-3 are addressed at plan level: fix_committed is Review and selected for PR polling; durable settlement protects reopened bugs from the historical PR; triaged predicates expose hold/failure; credential release is atomic and its lost-response/crash behavior is explicit, with a required-key guard. Revision-gated status synchronization also resolves the optimistic-update issue in finding 4. The remaining issues are:

1. [P1] Rollout step 3 still violates requester-key semantics (Rollout table, steps 2-4; I1/F3). S3b enables saving a key and queues params.llm actions, but the documented gate-off B4 path ignores those params and uses the project/environment key. An already allowlisted admin can therefore request a job through the new own-key flow and have it charged to the BOWIE key (and run with the wrong model). Draining at step 4 cannot undo calls already dispatched during step 3. Require B4 with its gate off to refuse requester-key-format actions instead of treating them as legacy, and/or keep new paid queueing disabled until B4's requester mode is enabled. State the coordinated activation sequence, including a stop/restart or quiescence boundary for in-flight old-mode tasks. Add a compatibility test with params.llm plus an allowlisted requester while the gate is off: zero model calls and zero env-key spend. Legacy operation before activation may remain explicit, but an action carrying the new own-key contract must never silently run through the old path.

2. [P2] Preserve reopen success across the inline crash boundary (§3 and Testing). The plan requires reopening with a closed->triaged CAS and refusing every other status. Phase 11 replays dispatched free inline actions after restart. If the process dies after that CAS but before _finish persists the action outcome, replay sees triaged and reports refused even though this action succeeded; the worker may also have advanced it beyond triaged. Existing close handles its simple repeat explicitly in run_inline. Specify durable action-correlated reopen evidence, or atomically persist the reopen transition and local action outcome, so recovery posts done without repeating the transition or mistaking an unrelated state change for success. Clear the old closure resolution_reason on successful reopen so a later manual close is not mislabeled merged. Add tests for crash after transition/before acknowledgment, replay after worker advancement, and a genuinely ineligible fresh reopen request.

The Anthropic terms check remains an explicit S3b release prerequisite, not a reviewed conclusion. Everything else from r1 is sufficiently specified for implementation review. Please revise documentation only and resubmit.

r3: both r2 findings addressed. Docs only; still uncommitted on docs/per-user-cloud-keys.

1 (P1, rollout / I1) — §Rollout rewritten.
- B4 with its gate OFF now refuses any paid action that carries `params.llm` ("per-user keys are not enabled on Bugalizer yet"). An own-key-format action never runs on the old path. Only legacy actions without params keep the allowlist + env-key rules.
- S3b ships own-key queueing behind a sonicgrid flag `BUGALIZER_USER_KEYS_ENABLED` (false = legacy format, paused = no paid buttons, true = params.llm + key required).
- Coordinated activation: (1) sonicgrid flag → paused; (2) quiesce BOWIE: /health triage_sync shows no held/dispatched paid actions, or their 45-min bound has passed; then stop the service; (3) gate on, allowlist env removed, start; (4) sonicgrid flag → true.
- Drain rules at the flip are as in r2.
- New compatibility test: gate off + params.llm + allowlisted requester → refused, zero complete() calls, zero env-key spend, endpoint never called. Plus tests for the flag's three values.

2 (P2, reopen across the inline crash boundary) — §3.
- New `db.reopen_for_action(report_id, action_id)`: ONE SQLite transaction does the CAS closed → triaged with `resolution_reason=NULL` (so a later manual close is not labelled merged), and, only if that matched, the same ledger write `triage_action_finish` performs (outcome done, expected_phase=dispatched).
- No match → nothing is written; the action is finished `refused` through the normal `_finish`.
- So a committed reopen is already finished in the ledger: recovery only posts it and never replays it, and a worker advancing the report afterwards can't turn it into a refusal. An uncommitted one changed nothing and is replayed against the real status.
- Tests: fresh closed → done and reason cleared; fresh triaged/rejected/duplicate → refused, unchanged; crash after commit before post → recovery posts done without a re-run; replay after the worker advanced past triaged → still done; crash before commit → replayed.

The file list is updated (reopen_for_action, ledger key_mode, the sonicgrid flag). The Anthropic terms check remains an S3b release prerequisite. No code, no tests.

Approved the round-3 plan in docs/phases/per-user-cloud-keys.md and its roadmap entry. All blocking findings from rounds 1 and 2 are addressed at plan level. No interjections or standing orders were delivered.

The mixed-version contract now refuses own-key-format actions while the Bugalizer gate is off, including allowlisted requesters, and documents coordinated activation with a service stop before enabling requester mode. Legacy actions remain explicitly distinguished and the gate-on drain cannot dispatch them on the env key. Reopen now clears the old resolution reason and commits the report transition together with the durable local action outcome, allowing recovery to post the recorded success even after subsequent worker advancement. The specified tests cover both fixes.

Earlier resolutions remain intact: real fix_committed PR lifecycle and durable settlement; actionable stage-detail precedence; atomic one-time credential release with explicit failure/crash handling and no env fallback; revision-gated status synchronization; cross-repo schema-first rollout.

Implementation checks to preserve the approved intent: enforce the paused queue flag in the server action as well as hiding buttons; roll back the entire reopen transaction if the expected-phase ledger write fails; establish that the old service process has actually exited at activation (an action timeout alone is not proof that its task stopped). These are consequences of the stated pause, atomicity and quiescence requirements, not additional product scope.

Documentation review only: read the complete revised plan and round-3 submission against the prior findings; no code edits or tests. The Anthropic terms check remains an unverified S3b release prerequisite. Approval is for the plan, not implementation or deployment, and this turn respects the docs-only instruction.
